verdict.rationale: Vue's releases page has a TypeScript Definitions policy. It warns that type definitions may break between minor versions and that Vue may raise the minimum required TypeScript version. It also recommends locking the Vue minor version to avoid breaks. However, the evidence never states which TypeScript versions are actually supported. Missing for 10: an explicit list of supported or minimum TypeScript versions, a per-Vue-release compatibility matrix, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I know which TypeScript versions the framework officially supports so I can avoid compatibility breaks when upgrading either one

citations.quote: Occasionally we may need to adopt features that are only available in a newer version of TypeScript, raising the minimum required version of TypeScript.
If you are using TypeScript, you can use a semver range that locks the current minor and manually upgrade when a new minor version of Vue is released.
